questions.question: Why is continuous workforce training important?
questions.reference_answer: It helps maintain workforce competency.
questions.evidence_phrase: Continuous professional development helps maintain workforce competency.

questions.question: Which psychological interventions are recommended for adults with moderate-to-severe depression?
questions.reference_answer: Behavioural activation therapy, brief psychodynamic therapy, cognitive behavioural therapy, interpersonal therapy, problem-solving therapy and third wave therapies.
questions.evidence_phrase: Structured psychological interventions should be offered for the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe depression, namely behavioural activation therapy (BAT), brief psychodynamic therapy (DYN), cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), interpersonal therapy (IPT), problem-solving therapy (PST) and third wave therapies (3WV).

questions.question: How long should antidepressant treatment continue after remission in adults with moderate-to-severe depression?
questions.reference_answer: For at least six months after remission.
questions.evidence_phrase: continuation of the antidepressant treatment should be considered for at least six months after remission.

questions.question: Which psychological interventions are recommended for adults with generalized anxiety disorder or panic disorder?
questions.reference_answer: Brief, structured psychological interventions based on cognitive behavioural therapy principles.
questions.evidence_phrase: Brief, structured psychological interventions based on principles of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) should be offered for adults with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) and/or panic disorder.

questions.question: Which psychological interventions can be considered for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.reference_answer: Trauma-focused CBT, digital or remote CBT, EMDR and stress management.
questions.evidence_phrase: Psychological interventions should be considered for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Namely, these include: individual face-to-face cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) with a trauma focus; group face-to-face CBT with a trauma focus; digital/remote CBT with a trauma focus; eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR); stress management.

questions.question: What intervention can be considered for individuals with thoughts or plans of self-harm?
questions.reference_answer: Safety planning-type interventions, including multicomponent interventions or those supplemented with follow-up or support.
questions.evidence_phrase: Safety planning type-interventions, i.e. interventions based on principles of safety planning which are multicomponent or supplemented with follow-up or support, can be considered.

questions.question: What are the key factors considered when determining the severity of depression?
questions.reference_answer: Symptoms, duration of the disorder, and the impact on personal and social functioning.
questions.evidence_phrase: Severity of depression is therefore a consequence of the contribution of all of these elements.

questions.question: Why should healthcare professionals ask people with depression about suicidal thoughts?
questions.reference_answer: To identify suicidal ideation and intent and assess the risk of self-harm or suicide.
questions.evidence_phrase: Always ask people with depression directly about suicidal ideation and intent.

questions.question: What factors should be considered when assessing a person with depression?
questions.reference_answer: Previous mental health history, supportive relationships, lifestyle, stressful life events, living conditions, and social isolation.
questions.evidence_phrase: Discuss with the person how the factors below may have affected the development, course and severity of their depression.

questions.question: How can regular physical activity help people with depression?
questions.reference_answer: Regular physical activity can enhance a person's sense of wellbeing, particularly when performed outdoors.
questions.evidence_phrase: The benefits can be greater if this activity is outdoors.

questions.question: Why is guided self-help considered as a first-line treatment for less severe depression?
questions.reference_answer: It is the least intrusive and least resource-intensive treatment option.
questions.evidence_phrase: consider the least intrusive and least resource intensive treatment first (guided self-help)

questions.question: What intervention should be offered first in the stepped-care model for GAD?
questions.reference_answer: The least intrusive, most effective intervention should be offered first.
questions.evidence_phrase: Follow the stepped-care model, offering the least intrusive, most effective intervention first.

questions.question: What should a comprehensive assessment of GAD consider besides the number, severity and duration of symptoms?
questions.reference_answer: It should consider the degree of distress and functional impairment.
questions.evidence_phrase: conduct a comprehensive assessment that does not rely solely on the number, severity and duration of symptoms, but also considers the degree of distress and functional impairment.

questions.question: Which low-intensity psychological interventions are recommended for people with GAD whose symptoms have not improved after education and active monitoring?
questions.reference_answer: Individual non-facilitated self-help, individual guided self-help and psychoeducational groups.
questions.evidence_phrase: individual non-facilitated self-help; individual guided self-help; psychoeducational groups.

questions.question: What psychological interventions should be offered when a person with GAD chooses high-intensity psychological treatment?
questions.reference_answer: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) or applied relaxation.
questions.evidence_phrase: If a person with GAD chooses a high-intensity psychological intervention, offer either CBT or applied relaxation.

questions.question: How long should a person with GAD continue taking medication if the drug treatment is effective?
questions.reference_answer: At least a year, because the likelihood of relapse is high.
questions.evidence_phrase: If the drug is effective, advise the person to continue taking it for at least a year as the likelihood of relapse is high.

questions.question: What are the common symptoms associated with post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.reference_answer: Re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, negative alterations in mood and thinking, emotional numbing, and dissociation.
questions.evidence_phrase: re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal (including hypervigilance, anger and irritability), negative alterations in mood and thinking, emotional numbing, dissociation

questions.question: What should healthcare professionals assess when evaluating a person with PTSD?
questions.reference_answer: Physical, psychological, and social needs, along with potential risks.
questions.evidence_phrase: Assessment of people with PTSD should be comprehensive, including an assessment of physical, psychological and social needs and a risk assessment.

questions.question: What treatment is recommended for adults with PTSD who present more than one month after a traumatic event?
questions.reference_answer: An individual trauma-focused cognitive behavioural therapy intervention.
questions.evidence_phrase: Offer an individual trauma-focused CBT intervention to adults with a diagnosis of PTSD or clinically important symptoms of PTSD who have presented more than 1 month after a traumatic event.

questions.question: How long should trauma-focused CBT typically be provided to adults with PTSD?
questions.reference_answer: Typically 8 to 12 sessions, with additional sessions if clinically indicated.
questions.evidence_phrase: typically be provided over 8 to 12 sessions, but more if clinically indicated, for example if they have experienced multiple traumas

questions.question: How should healthcare professionals support people with PTSD and complex needs?
questions.reference_answer: They should allow additional time to develop trust and address barriers to treatment engagement.
questions.evidence_phrase: build in extra time to develop trust with the person, by increasing the duration or the number of therapy sessions according to the person's needs

questions.question: What are the five key steps for implementing psychological interventions within an existing service?
questions.reference_answer: Planning, adaptation, workforce preparation, identification and assessment of beneficiaries, and monitoring and evaluation.
questions.evidence_phrase: make an implementation plan; adapt for context; prepare the workforce; identify, assess and support potential beneficiaries; and monitor and evaluate the service

questions.question: Why is community engagement important during the implementation of psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: It helps identify and overcome barriers to help-seeking and secure the buy-in of potential service users.
questions.evidence_phrase: community engagement is important to identify and overcome barriers to help-seeking and secure the buy-in of potential service users.

questions.question: How should providers be prepared to deliver psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: Providers should receive competency-based training and ongoing supervision.
questions.evidence_phrase: Equip providers with the right skills through competency-based training.

questions.question: Why is ongoing supportive supervision necessary for psychological intervention providers?
questions.reference_answer: It builds providers' confidence and competence, promotes safe and ethical practice, and encourages self-care.
questions.evidence_phrase: Ensure ongoing supportive supervision from appropriately experienced people to build providers’ confidence and competence, promote safe and ethical practice, provide support for challenging cases and encourage providers’ self-care.

questions.question: What is the purpose of monitoring and evaluation when implementing psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: To ensure interventions are not causing harm, assess whether they address mental health needs, and inform service improvements.
questions.evidence_phrase: ensure the intervention is not causing any harm; establish whether the psychological intervention is addressing the target population’s mental health needs; and inform adaptations and quality improvement strategies for the current service and future services implementing psychological interventions.

questions.question: What should be considered when planning treatment following self-harm?
questions.reference_answer: Associated coexisting conditions and the psychosocial assessment should be considered.
questions.evidence_phrase: When planning treatment following self-harm, take into account any associated coexisting conditions and the psychosocial assessment.

questions.question: What type of psychological intervention should be offered to adults who self-harm?
questions.reference_answer: A structured, person-centred, CBT-informed psychological intervention.
questions.evidence_phrase: Offer a structured, person-centred, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-informed psychological intervention (for example, CBT or problem-solving therapy) that is specifically tailored for adults who self-harm.

questions.question: What should a safety plan identify to help prevent further self-harm?
questions.reference_answer: Triggers, warning signs, coping strategies, social contacts and support.
questions.evidence_phrase: recognise the triggers and warning signs of increased distress, further self-harm or a suicidal crisis

questions.question: When should initial aftercare be provided if there are ongoing safety concerns?
questions.reference_answer: Within 48 hours of the psychosocial assessment.
questions.evidence_phrase: should provide initial aftercare within 48 hours of the psychosocial assessment.

questions.question: What should regular staff supervision promote when working with people who self-harm?
questions.reference_answer: Compassionate care, ongoing skill development, reflective practice, confidence and competence.
questions.evidence_phrase: promote the delivery of compassionate care

questions.question: Why does the manual use the term 'problem management' instead of 'problem-solving counselling'?
questions.reference_answer: It is used to help helpers and clients understand that even when problems are difficult or impossible to fully solve, there may still be ways to provide relief from their impact.
questions.evidence_phrase: By using the term "management", we hope that helpers and clients understand that when problems are challenging to solve there may still be ways to provide relief from their impact.

questions.question: What are the training requirements for helpers who are not mental health professionals?
questions.reference_answer: They must complete at least 80 hours (10 full days) of classroom training conducted by a competent mental health professional, followed by supervised in-field practice with at least two clients.
questions.evidence_phrase: The classroom training should be at least 80 hours (10 full days).

questions.question: How many sessions make up the Problem Management Plus (PM+) intervention and how long does each session last?
questions.reference_answer: The PM+ intervention consists of five 90-minute individual sessions, typically held once a week.
questions.evidence_phrase: PM+ is made up of five 90-minute individual sessions.

questions.question: Why should helpers generally avoid giving direct advice to clients during PM+?
questions.reference_answer: If a client relies on the helper's advice, they are unlikely to develop the ability to manage their own problems in the future once the intervention is over.
questions.evidence_phrase: If the client has been relying on your advice, they are unlikely to be able to manage their own problems in the future, when they have completed the PM+ intervention.

questions.question: What is the main goal of the 'Get Going, Keep Doing' strategy?
questions.reference_answer: It aims to break the cycle of inactivity and improve the client's mood by encouraging them to re-engage in pleasant and task-oriented activities regardless of their current mood.
questions.evidence_phrase: Get Going, Keep Doing aims to break this cycle and improve the client's mood by encouraging them to get involved again in pleasant and task-oriented activities in spite of their mood.

questions.question: What is the purpose of planning when implementing psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: Deciding which interventions will be provided, why, where, how and when.
questions.evidence_phrase: It involves deciding which interventions will be provided, why, where, how and when.

questions.question: How should psychological interventions be adapted for a specific context?
questions.reference_answer: By adapting the psychological interventions for use in a specific context, including translating them into local languages.
questions.evidence_phrase: Adapt the psychological interventions for use in a specific context, including translating them into local languages.

questions.question: How can a competent workforce be prepared to deliver psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: By selecting, training, assessing and supervising providers.
questions.evidence_phrase: Prepare and sustain a competent workforce to deliver the psychological interventions by selecting, training, assessing and supervising providers.

questions.question: Why is supportive supervision important for psychological intervention providers?
questions.reference_answer: To build providers’ confidence and competence, promote safe and ethical practice, provide support for challenging cases and encourage providers’ self-care.
questions.evidence_phrase: Ensure ongoing supportive supervision from appropriately experienced people to build providers’ confidence and competence, promote safe and ethical practice, provide support for challenging cases and encourage providers’ self-care.

questions.question: What are the three major steps involved in monitoring and evaluating psychological interventions?
questions.reference_answer: Make an M&E plan, collect and analyse data, and integrate findings.
questions.evidence_phrase: The process for monitoring and evaluating the integration of psychological interventions in existing services typically comprises three major steps: make an M&E plan based on the goals of integration; collect and analyse monitoring and/or evaluation data; and integrate findings to improve services or share lessons learned.
